description: A four-panel composite figure (genuinely mixed: grouped bar charts, tensile curves, and a literature property-comparison scatter) on three annealed low-density multiphase steels, AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T. (a) grouped bar chart of Volume fraction (%) (y axis 0–70) for phases F (red), B/TM (blue), FM (yellow) and RA (green): AN750-T = 49.3 / 35.0 / 8.3 / 7.4%, AN800-T = 46.8 / 44.2 / 6.6 / 2.4%, AN850-T = 54.7 / 41.4 / 3.3 / 0.6%. (b) grouped bar chart of Diameter (µm) (y axis 0–8), same legend and sample order: F = 4.53 / 5.14 / 5.35 µm, B/TM = 1.73 / 1.92 / 0.86 µm, FM = 1.06 / 0.42 / 0.40 µm, RA = 0.57 / 0.60 / 0.83 µm. (c) Engineering stress (MPa) versus Engineering strain (%) for AN750-T (blue), AN800-T (red) and AN850-T (black), with printed strength values 1068, 1269 and 1295 MPa and dashed elongation markers at 13.9%, 18.7% and 34.0%. (d) Tensile strength (MPa, x = 750–1350) versus Total elongation (%, y = 5–35) scatter of QP, DP, TRIP and TBF steels plus two red "Present steel" stars, separated by dashed PSE = 10, 20 and 30 GPa·% lines. Together the panels show that annealing temperature controls the F/B/TM/FM/RA balance and phase sizes, which sets the strength–ductility combination.

observations.observation: (a) Ferrite (F) volume fraction reads 49.3% (AN750-T), 46.8% (AN800-T) and 54.7% (AN850-T), i.e. not a strictly monotonic increase with annealing temperature.
(a) B/TM volume fraction reads 35.0%, 44.2% and 41.4%; FM reads 8.3%, 6.6%, 3.3%; RA reads 7.4%, 2.4%, 0.6% for AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T respectively.
(b) Ferrite diameter increases monotonically with annealing temperature: 4.53 µm (AN750-T), 5.14 µm (AN800-T), 5.35 µm (AN850-T).
(b) B/TM diameter reads 1.73, 1.92 and 0.86 µm; FM diameter 1.06, 0.42 and 0.40 µm; RA diameter 0.57, 0.60 and 0.83 µm for AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T.

(c) The blue curve labelled AN750-T has the lowest printed peak stress (1068 MPa) but the largest printed elongation (34.0%), whereas the 18.7% and 13.9% elongation markers belong to the higher-strength curves.

(c) Two high-strength values, 1295 MPa and 1269 MPa, are printed in red text with horizontal dashed guides alongside the blue 1068 MPa guide; the rendering does not unambiguously tie each red value to a single curve.
(d) The x axis is Tensile strength (MPa) covering roughly 750–1350 and the y axis is Total elongation (%) covering 5–35, with dashed boundary lines labelled PSE = 10, 20 and 30 GPa·%.
(d) Two red star markers for the 'Present steel' are plotted at high total elongation in the upper envelope of the comparison data, above most QP, DP and TBF steel points.

The caption identifies the panels as (a) phase volume fraction, (b) average size of phase, (c) tensile-curve data and (d) comparison of tensile strength–total elongation, with the reference markers 37-50 attached to panel (d).
The citing text states that as annealing temperature increases the ferrite content rises while bainite and martensite sizes decrease, based on Figs. 6(a) and (b).

The citing text states the multiphase steels show superior energy absorption during tensile deformation and yield strengths 2–3 times higher than traditional low-alloy steel, citing Figs. 6(c) and (d).

The citing text states no dynamic propagation instabilities such as Lüders bands or Portevin-Le Chatelier bands were observed in any sample, and that the average size of each phase was counted in Fig. 6(b) for use with the Hall-Petch relation.

subfigures.description: Grouped bar chart of Volume fraction (%) versus Sample for AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T; legend F (red), B/TM (blue), FM (yellow), RA (green). Printed values: AN750-T 49.3, 35.0, 8.3, 7.4; AN800-T 46.8, 44.2, 6.6, 2.4; AN850-T 54.7, 41.4, 3.3, 0.6.

Grouped bar chart of phase Diameter (µm) versus Sample (same three samples and same F/B/TM/FM/RA legend). Printed values: F 4.53, 5.14, 5.35; B/TM 1.73, 1.92, 0.86; FM 1.06, 0.42, 0.40; RA 0.57, 0.60, 0.83 for AN750-T, AN800-T, AN850-T respectively.

Engineering stress (MPa) versus Engineering strain (%) with three curves: blue AN750-T, red AN800-T, black AN850-T. Printed values 1295, 1269 (red text) and 1068 (blue text) with horizontal dashed guides, and dashed vertical elongation markers at 13.9% (black), 18.7% (red) and 34.0% (blue). The blue curve has the lowest peak stress but extends furthest in strain.

Tensile strength (MPa) versus Total elongation (%) property-comparison scatter, with markers for QP steel (grey squares), DP steel (blue circles), TRIP steel (green triangles), TBF steel (orange inverted triangles) and the Present steel (red stars), overlaid with three dashed iso-PSE lines labelled PSE = 30 GPa·% (blue), PSE = 20 GPa·% (red) and PSE = 10 GPa·% (black).
